summary: Neo Delay in Cross mode with its filters open: the first track's L. Length becomes Sync and Feel (or a free Time) and R. Length the right line's Offset; Feedback carries over to ±99 %; Dry thru and Wet out become a crossfade and an output gain.

rules.why: Lengths count in Length unit: ticks (the default) are Buzz's whole samples per tick, so the echo follows the tempo; a length in ticks that is a note value (1 tick = 1/16 at 4 ticks a beat, 3 ticks = 1/8 dotted, 6 = 1/4 dotted …) becomes Neo Delay's Sync and Feel, which follow the tempo too; any other length, and lengths in ms or samples, a free Time at the song's tempo and rate. R. Length becomes the right line's Offset (R ÷ L − 1, −50 … +100 %).
Both in %; each line's echo feeds the other line (its source's DoWork: left ← in + fb · right, right ← in + fb · left), as Neo Delay's Cross mode does; Neo Delay's stops at ±99 %.
Dry thru (on or off) and the echoes at Wet out (raw/128) add; Neo Delay crossfades them and sets the output's level: mix = wet ÷ (dry + wet), output = dry + wet.

remarks: Jeskola Cross Delay hears left + right summed (the input connections take +6 dB) and feeds that one signal into both lines; Neo Delay's Cross mode feeds each side's input into its own line, so a centred sound is the same and a panned one bounces from where it is.
Each of its tracks is a pair of lines of its own (up to 8); Neo Delay has one pair: the first track's settings move, the others' are left out.
Its Max Delay attribute (1 s by default) caps its lengths; the mapping doesn't read attributes.
